subject: Urgent: Dedicated pool surge causing throughput shortfall for StarkBank
messages:
From: Camille Dubois <camille.dubois@starkbank.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Latency + 500s & throughput drop on dedicated pool (production)

Team —

We started seeing a large increase in user-facing latency and 500 errors this morning on our production flows that depend on the reserved GPU pool you manage for us (commit: SB-ENTERPRISE-2026-09). P95 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.6s and our requests/second dropped by ~40% between 08:40–09:00 EST. We also saw a spike in error rates (5xx) and several timeouts in our downstream processors.

Attached is a short sample trace and a few request ids: req_3a2f, req_3a9b, req_3b10 — they consistently timeout when KV cache misses occur on long context prompts. Our platform is in rotation, but this is impacting checkout flows for a subset of customers.

We need: immediate mitigation (either temporary fallback to hosted capacity or an emergency scale-up), a timeline for remediation, and an understanding of whether this is a capacity/config issue on Redwood's dedicated pool. Please advise next steps and ETA.

Regards,
Camille
Head of ProdOps — StarkBank

Attachments: transaction-trace-018.log (log snippet, 45KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Camille Dubois <camille.dubois@starkbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:28:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Latency + 500s & throughput drop on dedicated pool (production)

Camille — thanks for the quick heads-up and the trace. I'm on it.

Immediate plan (starting now):
- Triage: Neha, please confirm whether the dedicated pool is saturated or if we have a software regression.
- Short-term mitigation: propose enabling burst capacity on the reserved pool and selectively routing non-critical traffic to our hosted fallback (same model, lower throughput SLA) to protect checkout flows. Marcus — I'll need you to own comms to the account on the fallback and billing implications.
- Observability: Marissa, please collect three customer request ids and any error correlation you have so we can look for common request shapes.

Camille — Can you confirm whether you want us to activate the hosted fallback automatically or do you prefer a controlled gradual switch? We'll hold on billing changes until we align.

I will follow up with a snapshot of pool allocation within 20 minutes.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Camille Dubois <camille.dubois@starkbank.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Latency + 500s & throughput drop on dedicated pool (production)

Quick update from infra — what I'm seeing in the metrics:
- Dedicated pool GPUs are at sustained 98–100% utilization across the node set for the 08:35–09:10 window.
- Request distribution shows several large-batch/long-context requests that cause disproportionate KV cache churn; sustained cache misses at seq>1024 are driving increased per-token compute and long tail latencies.
- There is a correlated increase in queueing (requests queued > 150ms) which explains the reduced rps.

Immediate mitigations I can execute if we agree:
1) Enable reserved pool burst (additional nodes from surge capacity) — will restore rps quickly (minutes) but will impact your committed billing unless we apply an emergency exception.
2) Turn on request shaping to limit large batch/concurrent bursts from non-critical routes for 30–60 minutes.
3) Prime KV cache for a small set of frequent prompts to reduce initial cold misses (manual warm-up script).

Attachments: pool-alloc-graph.png (pool allocation, 1.2MB)

If Camille gives the OK for (1) I'll kick it off now. If not, (2) + (3) will be our start. We should also open a follow-up postmortem to tune batching heuristics and eviction policy for the customer's usage pattern.

-Neha
SRE Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Camille Dubois <camille.dubois@starkbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 10:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Latency + 500s & throughput drop on dedicated pool (production)

Camille — apologies for the impact. We can take the following approach if you want the fastest recovery:
- I will authorize temporary burst capacity (Neha, please proceed). We will flag this as "emergency burst" and provide a capped dollar limit for StarkBank while we stabilize.
- Simultaneously enable a controlled fallback for lower-priority routes (we'll route to hosted endpoints) so critical checkout flows remain on the dedicated pool.
- Post-incident: we'll propose a tailored reserved pool sizing adjustment and a bandwidth protection policy to avoid recurrence.

Action items and timeline:
- 10:45 EST: Redwood enables burst + throttling (10–15 minute completion).
- 11:05 EST: initial stabilization check and customer confirmation.
- By EOD Mon: follow-up RCA kickoff and proposed sizing change.

DocuSign link for emergency burst amendment (internal use / approval): https://app.docusign.com/teams/starkbank-agreement

Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Executive Team <execs@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Camille Dubois <camille.dubois@starkbank.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Latency + 500s & throughput drop on dedicated pool (production) — request for exec awareness and credit consideration

Forwarding the thread — we escalated yesterday and applied emergency burst and request shaping; customer remains sensitive because this happened during peak settlement windows. Camille is requesting consideration for a credit for the incident window, plus an expedited sizing review.

Key points for execs:
- Impact window: ~08:40–09:20 EST on 2027-01-18; checkout flows degraded for an estimated 12% of checkout attempts for 30 mins.
- Actions taken: emergency burst (approved), KV priming, shaping, fallback routing. Stability restored by ~11:00 EST.
- Next steps: RCA (JIRA INF-4521), proposed committed capacity increase or a tailored protection policy.
- Ask: guidance on emergency credit and whether we should proactively offer a one-time bill credit and a short-term discounted surge window.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Camille Dubois <camille.dubois@starkbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 08:02:00 -0500
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — StarkBank dedicated pool incident (2027-01-18)

Camille — thanks again for patience. Summary of what we did and immediate next steps: 

What happened:
- A burst of large-context, high-token requests produced heavy KV cache churn and sustained GPU utilization that exhausted the dedicated pool's headroom. This drove queueing and increased error/timeout rates for ~40 minutes.

What we did (timeline):
- 09:28 EST: triage and mitigation options discussed.
- 10:45 EST: emergency burst capacity applied (surge nodes added) and request shaping enabled.
- 11:00 EST: observed stable rps and p95 reduced to baseline.

Short-term fixes applied:
- Burst capacity activation (manual emergency surge).
- Request shaping for non-critical routes (30–60 minute window).
- KV cache priming script run for top 20 prompts.

Follow-ups and commitments:
- RCA ticket opened: JIRA-INF-4521 (Neha owning technical RCA; target draft in 72 hours).
- Product follow-up: evaluate eviction policy and batching heuristics for reserved pools (product + infra).
- Commercial: Marcus to propose a one-time operational credit and discuss a revised reserved sizing option if you want guaranteed additional buffer.
- Postmortem meeting scheduled: Thu 2027-01-21 11:00 EST (calendar invite to follow).

Attachments: mitigation-playbook.pdf (internal post-incident checklist).

If you want us to revert the temporary burst (to avoid further billing exposure) we can schedule automated teardown after you sign the emergency amendment. Marcus — blocking on your doc send.

I'll keep you posted; open to any additional asks.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
